title: Conjecture 4
statement_text: Planar graphs have $r$-th weak coloring numbers in $O(r^2 \log r)$.
context_text: For a linear ordering $\sigma$ of $V(G)$ and $r\ge0$, a vertex $u$ is weakly $r$-reachable from $v$ if there is a $u$–$v$ path of length at most $r$ all of whose vertices $w$ satisfy $u\le_\sigma w$ (so $v$ itself is weakly reachable from $v$); $\mathrm{wcol}_r(G,\sigma)$ is the maximum over $v$ of the number of vertices weakly $r$-reachable from $v$, and the $r$-th weak coloring number $\mathrm{wcol}_r(G)$ is the minimum of $\mathrm{wcol}_r(G,\sigma)$ over all orderings, so that $\mathrm{wcol}_1(G)$ is the coloring number (degeneracy plus one). The conjecture concerns the maximum of $\mathrm{wcol}_r(G)$ over planar graphs $G$, as a function of $r$. Graphs of treewidth at most $k$ have $\mathrm{wcol}_r\le\binom{r+k}{k}$, tight (Grohe, Kreutzer, Rabinovich, Siebertz, Stavropoulos), giving planar graphs with $\mathrm{wcol}_r=\Omega(r^2)$; the best upper bound for planar graphs is $\binom{r+2}{2}(2r+1)=O(r^3)$ (Van den Heuvel, Ossona de Mendez, Quiroz, Rabinovich, Siebertz). The authors prove that graphs of simple treewidth at most $k$ (subgraphs of $k$-trees built without using any $k$-clique twice) have maximum $\mathrm{wcol}_r$ of order $\Theta(r^{k-1}\log r)$, which gives planar graphs with $\mathrm{wcol}_r=\Omega(r^2\log r)$ and the tight bound $\Theta(r\log r)$ for outerplanar graphs. They believe the lower bound is the right order for planar graphs. Similar gaps ($\Omega(p^2\log p)$ vs $O(p^3\log p)$) exist for the $p$-centered chromatic number and fractional treedepth-fragility rate of planar graphs.
